design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST: a Virginia non-owner insured convicted of a DUI in September (FR-44 filed in September on his 250/500/100 term, given its cancellation SR-26 while the term stood cancelled for nonpayment, and refiled after the reinstatement with lapse) asks for his renewal offer. The offer is not fixed until the term carries a package that accepts the conviction, so the agent must realign it to Non-Owner 100/300/50 (the insured's own election), book the premium re-written on the October reinstatement with lapse, book the increase charge for the realignment on the ledger basis, and only then issue the offer with its lapse-window factor.
SCOPE: task 1 claims nonowner_ext_reinstatement_rewritten (state_due, agent), nonowner_ext_package_rerate (state_due, user), nonowner_ext_package_increase_premium (state_due, agent) and nonowner_ext_renewal_offer_premium (on_request, root, agent).
DRAW: prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,6,4,5]; re-rate 6, renewal offer 5 (as drawn: increase 6, re-write 4).
PROBLEM TREE: root nonowner_ext_renewal_offer_premium <- nonowner_ext_package_rerate (state: 'The renewal offer premium is not fixed until the expiring term carries a package that accepts a DUI or DWI conviction within 60 months whenever the named insured has a DUI-related FR-44 Operator certificate requirement recorded.'); root <- nonowner_ext_package_increase_premium (action: 'A renewal offer is not issued before any increase charge owed for a package change made on the expiring term has been booked.'); nonowner_ext_package_increase_premium <- nonowner_ext_package_rerate (state: 'The increase charge for a package change is worked out only after the term carries the package it moves to.'); nonowner_ext_package_increase_premium <- nonowner_ext_reinstatement_rewritten (state: 'The increase charge is not worked out until the term's premium ledger carries a re-written premium entry for every reinstatement with a lapse recorded on the term.'). Skip runs: U -> offer 2192.66, increase 170.98; b -> increase 89.09.
FACTOR CARD re-write (expected 439.70, whole baseline 380.16): rewrite_lapse_relativity -> 414.81; rewrite_return_relativity -> 422.79; rewrite_plan_credit -> 453.30; rewrite_exposure_basis -> 406.51. Method: flat whole return (a certificate filed before the lapse and certified through its last day, here the first FR-44 until its certificate end date) vs certified-days amount (certification ends inside the lapse) vs per-day (no lapse day re-written).
FACTOR CARD re-rate (expected 2107.45, whole baseline 1143.04): rerate_filer_class -> 1561.07; rerate_lapse_relativity -> 1988.16; rerate_nonpay_relativity -> 1951.34; rerate_return_relativity -> 2026.39; rerate_plan_credit -> 2172.63; rerate_change_basis -> 1782.09. Method: max of current and new base (fewer than 15 days left) vs per-day blend (more than 60 days run, 15 or more left) vs flat new base.
FACTOR CARD increase (expected 64.89, whole baseline 0.00): increase_filer_class -> 0.00; increase_lapse_relativity -> 40.08; increase_nonpay_relativity -> 32.43; increase_return_relativity -> 48.03; increase_plan_credit -> 78.44; increase_deduction_basis -> 89.09. Method: ledger entry-by-entry deduction vs written premium over its own days vs written premium x increase days over term days.
FACTOR CARD offer (expected 1765.28, whole baseline 1211.62): offer_filer_class -> 1307.61; offer_nonpay_relativity -> 1634.52; offer_return_relativity -> 1697.38; offer_plan_credit -> 1819.88; offer_lapse_window -> 1782.09. Method: per-month share of the lapse relativity (3-5 day lapse, window ends inside the renewal) vs share floored at one half (6+ days) vs the standard flat relativity.
NEAR-MISSES: the withdrawn duplicate FR-44 (mistyped license) is not a requirement; the first FR-44 (cancellation_filed) counts for the lapse exposure but no longer as a requirement, the refiling being the requirement every filer class reads; the stale certificate field none; the rescinded July notice is not a cancellation; installment 4 fell due inside the lapse and is carried to the next invoice; an exclusive lapse count of 3 days stays in the 3-5 tier but 2 would not.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: re-write - nonowner_premium_charging.term_status; realignment - nonowner_eligibility.points, nonowner_lapse_attestation.policy_scope (overwritten for the DUI realignment, every other change restated); increase - term_status (premium_charging limits-increase sentence overwritten, reinstatement clause restated); offer - nonowner_renewal.policy_scope, nonowner_agg_multi_holding.
SEED: VA profile; one term (250/500/100, 1419.78), nonpayment cancellation 2026-10-10 and reinstatement with lapse 2026-10-14 (return 411.19 over 53 days); billing Six-Pay switched to Monthly EFT 2026-07-10 with the due day moved from the 2nd to the 12th, one returned draft 2026-09-16; fr FR-44 Operator filed 2026-09-22, cancellation SR-26 2026-10-12 (certificate end 2026-11-14), reinstatement refiling filed 2026-10-15, plus a withdrawn duplicate.
CROSS-CATEGORY SEED (fr / billing charters): first FR-44 Operator Certificate, VA, new requirement after the September DUI (DMV case recorded), requested 2026-09-21 while the term was in force (the nonpayment notice came on 2026-09-25) and filed 2026-09-22 within one business day on the 250/500/100 term, which lists Virginia among its FR-44 states; effective 2026-09-21; required through 2029-09-21; filing fee 35.00 billed on installment 4's draft notice of 2026-10-02. The term was cancelled for nonpayment on 2026-10-10 and was still cancelled, not yet reinstated, on 2026-10-12, so the SR-26 sent that day is the cancellation SR-26 (reason policy_cancelled), inside its window (closed date + 3 days), with the cancellation run-off: nonpayment, 2 days from the closed date to the SR-26 date within the 250/500/100 package's 30-day reinstatement window, so the larger of 10 and 30 - 2 = 28, plus Operator on a non-owner term 1, Virginia 4, filing state = residence 0, giving 33 days and certificate end 2026-11-14. The term was reinstated with a lapse after that SR-26, so the certificate was not revived and no further SR-26 is owed. The reinstated term needed a new filing: Dwayne ordered the reinstatement refiling on 2026-10-14 (carrying over form, state, case number and required-through date, naming the first filing as replaced); filed 2026-10-15, effective 2026-10-14; refiling fee 26.00 (the first certificate still certified on the refiling date, its certificate end being 2026-11-14, so half the 25.00 flat fee rounded up to 13; restoration after a lapse over 3 days 5.00; Operator on a non-owner term 2.00; Virginia 6.00; same state and no term form 0), charged to the plan and billed with the next invoice. Duplicate request of 2026-09-21 with a mistyped license number, withdrawn the same day before transmission; its 35.00 fee waived. Billing: first installment due 2026-07-02 (one month after the 2026-06-02 effective date), invoiced 20 days before, paid late 2026-07-09 with the 15.00 late fee after the 2026-07-07 notice; on 2026-07-10 the plan switched to Monthly EFT (recurring bank authorization signed that day, over 3 days before the next draft) and the due day moved by 10 days to the 12th (one change, requested 23 days ahead); draft notices 10 days before each due date; installment 3 drafted 2026-09-14 (due date a Saturday), returned 2026-09-16 with the 25.00 NSF fee, late fee 10.00 on 2026-09-18; final bill 2026-10-11 for the 348.31 balance after the return credit, its past-due part being installment 3's unpaid 266.16 (installment 4 was not yet due), with premium 43.15 (installment 4's premium and the unbilled last installment less the return credit) and fees 39.00 (installment 4's fee and the FR-44 filing fee, no new installment fee); reinstatement payment 266.16 on 2026-10-13, paying every past-due amount; plan reactivated.
PERSONA: chatty Richmond line cook; volunteers only the goal; credentials, the DUI and filing, and payment history only when asked; agrees to preliminary work after the agent explains it; runs the package change once with the values given; closes on the offer figure.
STANDARD SOLUTION: verify -> reads -> re-write 439.70 (53 days from 2026-10-10) -> user realigns to Cardinal Point Non-Owner 100/300/50 at 2107.45 -> increase 64.89 (45 days from 2026-10-18, additional premium with reason limits_decrease: the realignment lowers the base rate but its re-rated remaining days owe more than the ledger's unearned premium) -> renewal offer 1765.28 (2026-12-02..2027-06-02, 182 days). Re-write and realignment commute (both orders give identical values and world).
VERIFICATION: scratch harness (check_compute.build_env + real tool bodies on a dict world), per-factor baseline substitution, skip runs and the order swap; figures above are its output.
user_scenario: You are Dwayne Thibodeaux, thirty-seven, a line cook in Richmond who rides the bus and borrows a friend's car now and then; you own no car. You talk easily, a bit chatty, and you like to know what things will cost before you commit. Your Cardinal Point non-owner policy runs out on December 2, 2026, and you remember being told the renewal offer would be ready about six weeks ahead, but you have not seen it. You are calling to have your renewal offer put out today and to hear what the renewal premium is, so you can plan the payment; you are not paying anything on this call. You are happy for the representative to look into your account and to do whatever they need to do on their side for this, and if something is yours to do yourself, you will do it when they hand it to you. When the representative asks for details to find and verify you, you give your phone number, 8045555271, and your date of birth, 1988-11-05; if they want more, the last four of your driver's license are 5183 and your ZIP code is 23220. If they ask about your situation, you say you still do not own or lease a car, and nobody in your household has a car you use more than a day or two a week. If they ask about certificates with the state, you say you were convicted of a DUI in September, Virginia now requires an FR-44, and Cardinal Point filed it with the state for you in late September; after the policy was reinstated in October you had to order the filing again yourself, and Cardinal Point filed it the next day. If they ask about your payments, you say you paid the July bill about a week late, you switched to automatic bank drafts in mid-July and moved your due date to the 12th, a draft bounced in September, the policy got cancelled for a few days, and you paid what was owed online on October 13 to get it back. You do not know how premiums are figured and you never suggest a number. If the representative explains that something has to be done on your policy first, you say that is fine and to go ahead; when they tell you a step is one you have to put through yourself and give you the tool with the values to enter, you run it once with exactly those values and read back what it shows. Once you are told the renewal offer has been issued and what its full-term premium is, you thank them and end the call without asking for anything else.
